capex.item: IISCO/ISP expansion of about Rs 36,000 crore has major packages already ordered and ground activity started, with completion targeted in about three years (around FY30).
capex.quote: we have a project over there which is around Rs. 36,000 crores estimated. And most of the major packages have been already ordered out... They are going to finish in three years' time.

capex.item: SAIL will expand crude steel capacity from the current ~20 million tons to 35 million tons by 2030 through a mix of brownfield, debottlenecking and greenfield projects.
capex.quote: Right now, we are at around 20 million tons of capacity, and we want to go towards 35 million tons of capacity by 2030.

capex.item: Bhilai expansion of around 3.5 million tons at capex of about Rs 30,000 crores, being cleared now and yet to be formally announced, with majority of spend from FY29.
capex.quote: Bhilai, which is yet to be announced is around INR30,000 crores... At Bhilai, it will be around 3.5 million tons.

capex.item: Bokaro Steel Plant expansion of around 3 million tons at capex of about Rs 18,000 crores, cleared and following IISCO with majority of spend expected from FY29.
capex.quote: Bokaro is somewhere around INR18,000 crores... Bokaro also will be around 3 million tons.

capex.item: Total capacity expansion of 15 mt envisaged to become operational by 2031 at an indicative cost of Rs 1,10,000-1,20,000 crore.
capex.quote: the total expansion what we are expecting by 2031 is 15 mt... it would be in the range of 1,10,000 to 1,20,000 crores of 15 mt

capex.item: IISCO, Bokaro and Durgapur have Stage-I board approval for roughly 7.5 mt of combined capacity costing about Rs 55,000-56,000 crore, with costs being firmed up before Stage-II approval.
capex.quote: Bokaro and Durgapur Stage-I approval has also been given by the board... it will be roughly 7.5 mt all the three plants together... in the range of around 55,000 to 56,000 crores

capex.item: IISCO Steel Plant will add about 0.5 million tons brownfield capacity by FY27-FY28, with its full 7 million tons ultimate capacity coming by 2029.
capex.quote: in the brownfield, maybe around 0.5 million tons will come in ISP by that '27 or '28. But the entire 7 million tons ultimate capacity will come by 2029.

capex.item: A 4 million ton pellet plant is planned at Goa which will consume Jharkhand low-grade inventory and fresh fines in a 50:50 ratio initially.
capex.quote: we are planning a 4 million tons pellet plant at Goa itself, which will be consuming these low-grade as well as fresh fines in the ratio of 50%, 50% initially

capex.item: Rourkela and Bhilai are still awaiting Stage-I approval, with Rourkela expected to add roughly 3.5 mt and the balance coming at Durgapur in the second phase.
capex.quote: for this Rourkela and this Bhilai steel plant, we are still in the process of getting this first stage approval... roughly it will be in the range of Rourkela say around 3.5 mt additional

capex.item: To cut Durgapur's high semis content, SAIL plans a 1 mt TMT mill plus a 0.4 mt TMT mill, expected to take roughly three to four years once costs are firmed up.
capex.pv: 1 mt + 0.4 mt TMT mills in 3-4 years
capex.quote: we have a plan to bring down this 1 mt TMT mill and also on BU basis 0.4 mt TMT mill... roughly it will take another three to four years

capex.item: A 1 million tonne TMT bar mill at Durgapur Steel Plant has started ground work and is to be completed in about 18 months (18-24 months) followed by stabilisation and commissioning.
capex.quote: at Durgapur Steel Plant we have started one project which is 1-million-ton TMT bar mill... It will take 18 months' time. Ground work is already started.

capex.item: Beyond the TMT mill, an approved package at Durgapur (new blast furnace, converter and caster replacing the old blast furnace) will raise Durgapur hot metal and crude steel capacity by 1 million tonnes.
capex.quote: beyond TMT mill, we have also approved another package for them. And which will also increase the overall capacity of Durgapur Steel Plant by 1 million tonnes.

capex.item: Pellet plants are being set up on a BOO basis with SAIL bearing only O&M cost; the Bhilai mines plant starts around end-May/June 2025 while Rourkela and Durgapur plants are at tendering stage and will take up to 3 years.
capex.quote: At Bhilai mines, it is going to start after a month, this month, May end, or June... in Rourkela and Durgapur, they are at the tendering stage... It will take around 3 years

capex.item: A new TMT bar mill at Durgapur Steel Plant will be commissioned in about 2.5 years, after which semis are expected to be almost zero or negligible.
capex.quote: we're going to put up a new TMT bar mill at Durgapur steel plant, so which will come after 2.5 years. So at that time, you look at the semis, it will be almost kind of zero

capex.item: SAIL plans to convert the sub-grade Goa iron ore fines into pellets but has yet to obtain Stage-I board approval; the board note is still being framed.
capex.quote: For conversion of that into the pelletization, we are yet to get this first stage approval from the board... the plan is there to convert it to pellet

capex.item: Peak capex is expected around FY28-FY29 and could rise to roughly INR10,000-15,000 crores from the current INR7,500 crores.
capex.quote: this peak level of -- this capex may happen sometime around maybe... around '28, '29... If it is INR7,500 crores today, so it may increase by around INR10,000 crores, INR15,000 crores

capex.item: Debottlenecking projects are expected to add roughly 2-3 million tons of capacity by 2028.
capex.quote: in that process of debottlenecking, by 2028, we are expecting to increase it by maybe around 2 million to 3 million tons

capex.item: Brownfield and debottlenecking work at Durgapur, Bhilai and Rourkela steel plants will add 1-1.5 million tons of capacity by 2028, with greenfield projects at these plants delivering benefits by 2030.
capex.quote: this will also add capacities of 1 million to 1.5 million tons by 2028... all of these are geared up towards giving benefits by 2030.

capex.item: IISCO expansion spend in FY27 will be around Rs 7,000-8,000 crore, with the peak outgo in FY28 and FY29.
capex.quote: IISCO amount could be maybe around 7,000 to 8,000 crores in case of IISCO so far as 2026-2027 is concerned

capex.item: IISCO Steel Plant expansion of about 4.5 million tons at a capex of roughly Rs 35,000-36,000 crores; major packages already tendered and firmed up, groundwork starting with a bit of spend in Q4FY27 and expenditure ramping from FY28.
capex.quote: capex of IISCO is around INR36,000 crores -- maybe INR35,000 crores... Corresponding capacity in IISCO is around 4.5 million tons.

capex.item: New expansion capacity will only start coming online after three years, i.e. from FY31; until then growth comes from debottlenecking and operational efficiency, with volumes able to stretch to about 23 million tons.
capex.quote: New capacity will start coming after 3 years from now, means from '30-'31.

bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Debt reduction (targeting further decrease in Net Debt/Equity below 0.37); Priority 2: Funding organic capacity expansion (IISCO, Bokaro, Bhilai); Priority 3: Divestment of BISL (on disinvestment list); No major M&A planned, focus on brownfield growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical volatility in Middle East affecting fuel/raw material logistics; Pending government guidelines on Pay Commission revision (potential cost spike in FY27); Rail price revision uncertainty for FY27 (provisional pricing currently); Monsoon season impact on Q2 demand and inventory buildup; Chiria mine lease approval delays.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and optimistic; Emphasized 'clean balance sheet' with no auditor qualifications for the first time in decades; Focused on operational excellence driving volumes beyond theoretical capacity; Pragmatic on cost inflation but confident in offsetting via efficiency.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: SAIL is operating blast furnaces beyond theoretical DPR capacities (productivity 3.0 vs design 2.3) via operational enablers, a trend industry-wide but critical for SAIL's near-term volume growth without greenfield capex; The INR 1,800 Cr rail price arrear benefit in FY25 created a high base, making FY26's 51% PAT growth purely operational and more sustainable; Third-party trading (RINL/NSL) is being phased out/adjusted, with FY27 guidance of 22 MT excluding most third-party volumes to reflect true organic growth.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Borrowings (non Ind-AS) have been reduced from Rs. 29,811 crore in Mar'25 to Rs. 21,729 crore in Jun'26, a consistent quarter-on-quarter deleveraging.
- Debt-equity has fallen from 0.54x in Mar'25 to 0.36x in Jun'26 on a non Ind-AS basis, with the Ind-AS debt-equity at 0.54.
- Net worth has expanded from Rs. 55,656 crore in Mar'25 to Rs. 59,720 crore in Jun'26, so deleveraging is being achieved through retained earnings rather than asset sales.
- Quarterly interest cost has come down from Rs. 664 crore in Mar'25 to Rs. 493 crore in Jun'26, and coverage metrics stand at DSCR 1.66 and interest coverage 4.80.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Long Products NSR: INR 53,400/ton (Q4) -> INR 57,800/ton (May); Flat Products NSR: INR 51,000/ton (Q4) -> INR 56,000/ton (May); Bokaro Plant: Sharp EBITDA recovery post-capital repairs on Hot Strip Mill and SMS issues resolved; Salem Steel Plant: Still loss-making, targeting yield improvement (84% to 90%) and fuel switching to reduce bleeding.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraints and high input costs limiting sector growth | Tata Steel | beneficiary | Med | SAIL's aggressive capex and volume growth validates the domestic steel demand story, potentially lifting sector valuations, though Tata Steel faces its own coal cost pressures. |
| Rail infrastructure demand outpacing supply | JSW Steel | beneficiary | Med | SAIL's focus on long products and rails highlights the robustness of the infrastructure theme, benefiting peers with flat product exposure looking to diversify or capture spill-over demand. |
| High coking coal prices squeezing margins across the board | JSPL | loser | Low | While SAIL mitigates via mining integration, peers with lower captive mining ratios may face steeper margin compression from the INR 2,000/ton coal price hike mentioned. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- SAIL is presented as a fully integrated producer spanning its own mining (10.410 MT iron ore, 0.242 MT limestone and 0.140 MT dolomite in the quarter) through to hot metal, crude steel and finished steel, giving it raw-material backward integration rather than dependence on purchased ore.
- Output is anchored on five Integrated Steel Plants (BSP, BSL, RSP, DSP and ISP) plus special/alloy steel units (SSP, ASP, VISL), a multi-plant footprint the deck treats as the core of the franchise.
- The deck frames SAIL against a domestic backdrop where Indian crude steel production rose ~3% and finished steel consumption ~8% year-on-year in Q1 FY27, positioning the company as a leveraged play on India's infrastructure- and capital-goods-led demand.
- Sales are overwhelmingly domestic: home sales were 93.6% of the mix and exports only ~1.4%, so the business is structurally an India-demand story rather than an export arbitrage one.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Channel mix] Distribution is dominated by non-retail institutional sales at 86.2%, with retail only 7.4% and plant sales 3.3% - a structurally project- and OEM-driven customer base.
- [Rail pricing] The EBITDA bridge separately calls out a 'Rail Price Adjustment' line as a distinct swing factor between quarters, reflecting SAIL's exposure to administered railway product pricing.
- [Global backdrop] The deck notes China still accounts for ~53.7% of world crude steel production (Jan-May CY26) even while its own output fell 3.8%, framing persistent global oversupply risk.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Coking coal cost rose from INR 18,200/ton (Q4) to INR 21,800/ton (May); Offset by INR 429 Cr gain from raw material usage efficiency (higher PCI, oxygen injection); Flux costs up slightly due to Middle East logistics ($23 to $35/ton) but marginal impact (INR 100-200/ton); Employee cost trending down due to natural attrition (3,400 reduction FY26) despite pending pay commission revision (due Jan 2027).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Targeting 22 MT sales volume in FY27 (excl. third-party); Margins: Expected to improve despite INR 2,000/ton coking coal hike due to operational gains; Order Inflow: Steady domestic demand, export opportunities firming; Capex: INR 15,000 Cr (FY27), INR 18,000-19,000 Cr (FY28), rising to INR 20,000-25,000 Cr annually during peak expansion.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Sales volume guidance of 22.5 MT for FY27 (including ~0.6-0.7 MT from RINL); Crude steel production target 22.5 MT against 21 MT installed capacity (operating >100% via debottlenecking); Inventory reduced by 0.9 MT in FY26, targeting flat inventory in Q1 FY27.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Brownfield expansions: IISCO (+4.5 MT, INR 35k Cr capex), Bhilai (+3.5 MT, INR 30k Cr capex), Bokaro (+3 MT, INR 18k Cr capex); New capacity online from FY31; Mining ramp-up from 38 MT to 80 MT long-term; Chiria mine lease acquisition pending.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SAIL delivered a record clean balance sheet with zero auditor qualifications and massive debt reduction (INR 8,150 Cr FY26) driven by inventory liquidation and operational efficiency, setting the stage for an aggressive capex cycle (INR 15k-25k Cr/year) to expand capacity beyond 22.5 MT via debottlenecking and brownfield expansions at IISCO, Bokaro, and Bhilai.

open.item: Total inventory stands at 2.4 million tonnes (1.5 mt finished, 0.9 mt in-process) versus 2.7 mt at 31 March, and management expects a further 0.3 million tonne reduction in each of February and March.
open.promised: 0.3 per month in Feb and Mar million tonnes

open.item: FY26 sales volume is guided at around 19.5 million tonnes including NSL (about 18.5 million tonnes on SAIL's own steel), with Q4 volumes higher than Q3's 5.15 million tonnes.
EBITDA per tonne is currently around Rs 6,000-7,000 and management expects Q4FY26 to be better than that, with margins remaining good on price uptick despite high coal prices.

Borrowings were cut by about Rs 5,000 crore in 9MFY26 plus about Rs 2,000 crore in January, and management says the reduction momentum continues through February and March with borrowings going down drastically in Q4.
Interest cost fell by Rs 500 crore in 9MFY26 and a further Rs 500 crore reduction is expected in Q4, taking full-year FY26 interest cost reduction to around Rs 1,000 crore.

Coking coal consumption cost is set to rise about Rs 1,500 per tonne in Q4FY26 over Q3's Rs 18,351 (Jan Rs 18,500, Feb Rs 19,700, another Rs 1,000 in March), with the $251/t spot index also flowing into April.

Domestic price increases of about Rs 2,000-2,500 per tonne in longs and Rs 3,300-3,500 per tonne in flats reflected in January, and management guides sales realisation to move further up in February and March.

After the Bokaro converter tube leakage and the Bhilai SMS spillover (which cost about 2,000 tonnes per day of hot metal for 15-16 days), all five integrated plants are back at 98-100%+ levels and management says there will be no such problem in Q4.
FY26 revenue, which had been stuck at around Rs 1 lakh crore in earlier years, will be a materially bigger number this year (9M revenue already Rs 79,997 crore, up 9%).
FY26 capex will land between the initial guidance of Rs 7,500 crore and the final guidance of Rs 10,000 crore, against Rs 5,428 crore spent in 9MFY26.
SAIL is targeting semi-finished steel at less than 14% of volumes in FY26, aiming for roughly 10-12%, versus ~15% currently.
Capex for FY26 has been fixed at INR7,500 crores, excluding pellet plants which are on a BOO basis.
Crude steel production in FY26 is targeted at around 20 million tons or beyond, versus 19.17 million tons in FY25.
With 20 million tons crude steel in FY26, saleable steel would be around 19.2-19.3 million tons and sales are targeted at more than that level.
open.promised: more than 19.2-19.3 million tons million tons

open.item: Employee cost is expected to fall by at least INR400-500 crores in FY26 due to natural separations, with a normalised quarterly run-rate of about INR2,900 crores.
open.promised: INR400 to INR500 crores reduction INR cr

open.item: Techno-economic parameter improvements delivered around INR650 crores of cost benefit in FY25 and management is targeting a higher cost-reduction number in FY26.
open.promised: more than INR650 crores INR cr

open.item: Blast furnace productivity averaged 2.02 tons per cubic meter per day in FY25 versus 1.88 and is expected to go beyond 2 again in FY26, with coke rate already down to 421 kg per ton of hot metal.

Borrowings, at about INR26,700-26,800 crores currently versus INR29,811 crores at March 2025, are planned to be reduced further month-on-month during FY26, funding capex through internal accruals plus other instruments.
FY26 capex is guided at roughly Rs 7,500 crore as expansion capex starts flowing.

Imported coking coal prices have risen from a Q4FY26 average of about Rs 19,500 to roughly Rs 21,500, an increase of about Rs 2,000, which management expects to translate into a cost-of-production impact of Rs 1,400-1,500 per ton in Q1FY27, partly cushioned by ~30 days of cheaper stock and supportive NSR.

verdicts.item: Management committed to bring total borrowings by end-FY25 back to the 31st March 2024 level of about Rs 30,500 crore, from Rs 32,600 crore currently.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: FY25 capex target of Rs 5,700 crore, of which Rs 3,900 crore was spent to December, leaving Rs 1,800 crore for Q4FY25.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Crude steel production for FY25 is running at around 18.5 mt.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Full-year FY25 saleable steel sales target of about 17.5 mt, with 1.57 mt achieved in January.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Coal blend cost, at Rs 19,200 per ton in Q3, is expected to fall by roughly another Rs 1,000 per ton in Q4FY25 as imported coal prices decline from Rs 20,000 to about Rs 19,000 per ton.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Management expects steel prices to have bottomed out and realisation and margins to improve in Q4FY25, the seasonally strongest quarter, particularly in flats; January blended NSR was Rs 48,400 per ton versus Rs 49,700 in Q3.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 4Q past horizon Q4FY25

verdicts.item: Management expects margins to improve in coming quarters, with NSR up roughly INR2,000-3,000 per ton in Q1FY26 over Q4FY25 post safeguard duty, though it is market driven and monsoon will keep prices subdued before a post-monsoon improvement.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 3Q past horizon Q1FY26

capital_allocation.body: Priority 1: Debt reduction (targeting further decrease in Net Debt/Equity below 0.37); Priority 2: Funding organic capacity expansion (IISCO, Bokaro, Bhilai); Priority 3: Divestment of BISL (on disinvestment list); No major M&A planned, focus on brownfield growth.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident and optimistic; Emphasized 'clean balance sheet' with no auditor qualifications for the first time in decades; Focused on operational excellence driving volumes beyond theoretical capacity; Pragmatic on cost inflation but confident in offsetting via efficiency.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical volatility in Middle East affecting fuel/raw material logistics; Pending government guidelines on Pay Commission revision (potential cost spike in FY27); Rail price revision uncertainty for FY27 (provisional pricing currently); Monsoon season impact on Q2 demand and inventory buildup; Chiria mine lease approval delays.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: SAIL is operating blast furnaces beyond theoretical DPR capacities (productivity 3.0 vs design 2.3) via operational enablers, a trend industry-wide but critical for SAIL's near-term volume growth without greenfield capex; The INR 1,800 Cr rail price arrear benefit in FY25 created a high base, making FY26's 51% PAT growth purely operational and more sustainable; Third-party trading (RINL/NSL) is being phased out/adjusted, with FY27 guidance of 22 MT excluding most third-party volumes to reflect true organic growth.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capacity constraints and high input costs limiting sector growth | Tata Steel | beneficiary | Med | SAIL's aggressive capex and volume growth validates the domestic steel demand story, potentially lifting sector valuations, though Tata Steel faces its own coal cost pressures. |
| Rail infrastructure demand outpacing supply | JSW Steel | beneficiary | Med | SAIL's focus on long products and rails highlights the robustness of the infrastructure theme, benefiting peers with flat product exposure looking to diversify or capture spill-over demand. |
| High coking coal prices squeezing margins across the board | JSPL | loser | Low | While SAIL mitigates via mining integration, peers with lower captive mining ratios may face steeper margin compression from the INR 2,000/ton coal price hike mentioned. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Channel mix] Distribution is dominated by non-retail institutional sales at 86.2%, with retail only 7.4% and plant sales 3.3% - a structurally project- and OEM-driven customer base.
- [Rail pricing] The EBITDA bridge separately calls out a 'Rail Price Adjustment' line as a distinct swing factor between quarters, reflecting SAIL's exposure to administered railway product pricing.
- [Global backdrop] The deck notes China still accounts for ~53.7% of world crude steel production (Jan-May CY26) even while its own output fell 3.8%, framing persistent global oversupply risk.

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.
